title: routing-policy-escalation-matrix-and-simulation-notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures an operational runbook embedded in architecture guidance for our control-plane routing policies across regions. Intended readers: platform engineers, SREs, and on-call rotations who own routing policy distribution, state reconciliation, and multi-region failover behavior.

High-level problem statement:
When control-plane state diverges from dataplane policy (reason: partition, slow propagation, or buggy rollout), we see transient or sustained blackholes, route flapping, and customer-requested fallbacks. This doc ties routing policy design decisions to practical incident scenarios and prescribes an escalation matrix, deterministic remediation steps, and game-day simulation checklists.

Key primitives and assumptions:
- Control plane pushes policy bundles (route maps, priority lists, model-variant routing) to region controllers via gRPC multiplexed streams.
- Each region maintains a local policy cache and an applied-version ledger (applied_version, last_applied_ts).
- Heartbeat and compacted snapshot checkpoints every 30s; deltas streamed thereafter.
- Immutable model variants are referenced by digest; compatible fallbacks are encoded in the policy meta.
- Operators may trigger manual overrides via Console or CLI; overrides write to an override namespace that has precedence.

Metrics and SLOs to watch during incidents:
- policy_apply_latency_p50/p95/p99 (controlplane->region)
- policy_apply_error_rate (per-region)
- route_reject_rate (client-facing 5xx mapped to routing)
- KV_cache_divergence_count (differences between expected ledger and dataplane snapshot)
- request_fallback_rate (percentage routed to fallback model/region)
- inter_region_controlplane_rtt

Incident types and triggered alerts (examples):
1) Stale policy ledger in region (alert: KV_cache_divergence_count > 0 for > 120s)
   Observable symptoms: unchanged applied_version while controlplane shows newer version; customers in region see elevated 5xx or model regression.
   Immediate impact: incorrect routing, inability to access newly-rolled models or targeted throttles.

2) Partial control-plane partition (alert: inter_region_controlplane_rtt increased AND policy_apply_error_rate spike)
   Symptoms: some regions apply changes slowly, others fast; routing inconsistency across regions; occasional split-brain override conflicts.

3) Policy regression from a rollout (alert: route_reject_rate spike coincident with deploy tag)
   Symptoms: sudden route drop for a subset of customer tokens; increased fallback to default model.

4) Oscillating DNS/edge routing causing flapping (alert: client connection count oscillations + route change events)
   Symptoms: client reconns, timeouts, cache thrash.

Escalation matrix (decision tree text):
- Tier 0 (on-call platform engineer): verify alerts, gather metrics, check applied_version, check console overrides. If KV_cache_divergence_count > 0, run local reconciliation step (Step A). If simple rollout regression and can rollback via Console within 2 minutes, perform rollback.
- Tier 1 (senior platform eng): if Step A fails or partition detected, escalate to Tier 1. Tier 1 reviews control-plane cluster health, ETCD/consensus state, and network ACLs. If consensus unhealthy, initiate leader re-election or promote standby cluster.
- Tier 2 (platform lead + SRE): if manual fixes cause customer impact > 15 minutes or repeated flaps, open incident bridge, notify affected PMs/CS, and prepare cross-region traffic migration plan.

Concrete runbook steps (flat deterministic commands and checks):
Step A: Fast reconciliation for stale applied_version
- 1) Run: ./scripts/controlplane/check_applied_versions.sh --region <region> 
- 2) Check leader log: kubectl -n controlplane logs deploy/controlplane-leader -c applier --since=10m | grep "apply_error"
- 3) If applier process shows OOM or crashloop: kubectl rollout restart deploy/controlplane-applier -n controlplane --timeout=5m
- 4) If restart does not clear divergence in 90s, run: ./scripts/controlplane/force_snapshot_push.sh --region <region> --target-version <controlplane_version_digest>
- 5) Post-check: curl -sS http://<region-controller>/metrics | grep applied_version ; expect >= controlplane_version_digest

Step B: Partitioned control plane (partial region visibility)
- 1) Confirm network ACLs: gcloud compute firewall-rules list --filter="name~'cp-.*'" or aws ec2 describe-network-acls --region <region>
- 2) Validate etcd consensus: kubectl exec -n controlplane etcd-0 -- etcdctl endpoint status --cluster
- 3) If 2/3 etcd members unhealthy: add resource pressure action: scale controlplane statefulset replicas from N to N+1 in a region with low load (kubectl scale sts controlplane --replicas=<n+1>)
- 4) If metrics show heartbeat re-established, run Step A reconciliation.

Step C: Rollout regression rollback
- 1) Identify deploy tag from CI: check linked_artifacts or ci pipeline: https://ci.redwood.internal/pipelines/
- 2) If deployment < 15 minutes ago and rollback window open: Console -> Rollouts -> Select policy bundle -> Rollback to previous stable version.
- 3) If Console is unresponsive, use CLI: rwectl policy rollback --bundle <previous_digest> --regions <affected_regions> --force
- 4) Monitor route_reject_rate and route_success_rate for 10 minutes.

Step D: Cross-region traffic migration (hard mitigation)
- Preconditions: Tier 2 approval, run during maintenance window or after stakeholder notification.
- 1) Whitelist customers: construct migration list via query against tenant routing map.
- 2) Apply migration policy with gradual weight shift: rwectl traffic shift --from-region <bad> --to-region <good> --tenants-file migration-list.csv --rate 5%/min
- 3) Observe latency and success percent; roll back migration if per-tenant p50 latency increases > 50ms or error rate > 2x baseline.

Safety and invariants (to avoid cascading failures):
- Never apply a global "force override" across all regions unless Tier 2 approves.
- Prefer increasing fallback rate to a cached stable model over forcing a new policy bundle when propagation is uncertain.
- All force_snapshot_push and rollback actions must be logged to incident channel and annotated in the policy audit log.

Escalation channel templates (Slack snippets):
- When escalating to Tier 1: "@platform-tier1 seeing policy_apply_error_rate=12% and KV_cache_divergence_count=3 in us-west-2. Current applied_version=sha:abcd, controlplane target=sha:ef01. Running Step A (reconciliation). Joining bridge: <bridge link>"
- When moving to cross-region migration: "INCIDENT PRIORITY P1: initiating controlled traffic migration from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for affected tenants. Tier 2 approval granted by @lead. Link to migration tracker: <sheet link>"

Game-day simulation checklist (run quarterly):
- 1) Simulate a policy bundle regression: deploy canary policy to a single region and assert correct rollback cadence and alerts.
- 2) Simulate control-plane partition by blocking gRPC between one region controller pair for 120s and validate reconciliation behaves per Step B.
- 3) Run chaos experiment for instance restarts of applier pods during high apply load. Confirm time-to-recover < 180s.
- 4) Validate cross-region migration script on staging with synthetic tenants and confirm no data leak in audit logs.

Open questions and action items:
- Q1: Should rollback be automated for specific class of policy regressions? Action: experiment in staging with limited automation and revertibility (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2025-01-15).
- Q2: Improve observability of ledger deltas: ship per-delta diff logs to centralized bigquery + a dashboard (owner: Sofia Ramirez, due: 2025-03-01).

Appendix A: Quick commands reference
- check versions: ./scripts/controlplane/check_applied_versions.sh --region <r>
- force snapshot: ./scripts/controlplane/force_snapshot_push.sh --region <r> --target-version <v>
- list control plane pods: kubectl get pods -n controlplane -o wide
- tail applier logs: kubectl -n controlplane logs deploy/controlplane-applier -c applier -f

Appendix B: Contact matrix
- Platform Tier 0: rotation@redwood-inference.com (primary: Asha Patel)
- Platform Tier 1: leads@redwood-inference.com (primary: Marco Chen)
- Product/CS notify list: product-alerts@redwood.com

Notes on uniqueness: this doc focuses on embedding deterministic runbook steps directly with architectural checks and a simulation schedule. It privileges explicit commands and decision boundaries (e.g., thresholds for KV_cache_divergence_count and allowed rollback windows) to reduce ambiguity during on-call.
